evidence: Reviewed deterministic logging as a counterexample to same-input/same-output sufficiency.

Reviewed clock capability versus timestamp value and repository capability versus versioned snapshot.
Reviewed mutable argument alias as a counterexample to syntactic explicitness.
Reviewed memoization proof obligation and the incomplete-key counterexample.
Confirmed no universal effect-safety or host-language purity proof is claimed.
proof_review.notes: Proofs and counterexamples are relative to declared observations, domains and implementation versions.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter deepens FP-001 by defining input completeness and world noninterference, separates adjacent properties, and reserves higher-order functions, closures, effect composition, reader/state abstractions, I/O boundaries and property-based testing for their later modules.

practitioner_review.notes: Production guidance covers configuration and reference snapshots, capabilities, clocks, random state, failure values, mutable aliases, cache keys, replay versions, command descriptions, resource qualifications, pure-core/effectful-shell ownership and high-stakes fail-closed boundaries.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten examples and five exercises progressing from a minimal pure function through logging, time, randomness, mutation, memoization, closures and command data to clinical counterexamples and service-boundary redesign.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
